LITERATURE IN ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

2. When practising Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.

3. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. No full stops
   D. Only one word repeated

4. When practising Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.

5. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. quickly
   C. run
   D. blue

6. When practising Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.

7. When practising Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - , which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .
   C. Copy random text without understanding Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .
   D. Use insults to “practise” Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .

   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .
   C. Use insults to “practise” Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .
   D. Copy random text without understanding Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .

9. When practising Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.

   C. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla.

11. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. went
   C. goes
   D. going

12. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only a describing word
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only an action

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Non- fiction: Autobiography - Writing - Values in non- fiction - Culture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Oral Literature 8.1.1 Songs/Oral Poetry Initiation songs -Form -Subject matter - and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Poetry 8.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Language and Style: - Imagery - Simile - Met and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Fiction and Non- Fiction 8.3.1 Fiction: The Play from Kenya - Performing a play  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Where is the library?

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.

3. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

4. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.

5. C — run

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla.

11. B — went

12. C — A person, place, thing, or idea

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Non- fiction: Autobiography - Writing - Values in non- fiction - Culture; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Oral Literature 8.1.1 Songs/Oral Poetry Initiation songs -Form -Subject matter -; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Poetry 8.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Language and Style: - Imagery - Simile - Met; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Fiction and Non- Fiction 8.3.1 Fiction: The Play from Kenya - Performing a play ; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
